articles.body: Table of Contents Where Your Password Rules Came From Myth 1: Composition Rules Make Passwords Stronger Myth 2: Passwords Must Expire Every 90 Days Myth 3: Complex Beats Long Myth 4: Strength Meters Know Best Myth 5: Security Questions and Hints Add Protection What NIST Recommends Now What This Means for You Where Your Password Rules Came From The password requirements you have memorized - at least 8 characters, must contain uppercase, lowercase, a digit and a symbol, replace it every 90 days, never reuse the last five - can be traced largely to a single document: NIST Special Publication 800-63 from 2003, written by engineer Bill Burr. articles.body: On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere . After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets , the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were launched. Those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space .
